answer: A credible agent economy can price entry through deferred rewards instead of upfront fees. New nodes earn nothing for their first epochs; payouts vest gradually, so a sybil farmer who spawns a thousand disguised wallets funds a thousand idle machines while honest agents compound. Trust here behaves like an ember: it starts small, must be tended through verified work, and cannot be bought at scale. Watchdogs act as ravens, circling the network and reporting collusion for slashing. What emerges is an oasis of verified agents - slow to join, hard to fake, expensive to betray.
